title: Chapter 77 — The Great Heidelburgh Tun
paragraphs: Now comes the baling of the case. But to understand it properly, you must know something of the curious internal structure of the thing being operated upon.

Regarding the Sperm Whale's head as a solid rectangle, you may, on an inclined plane, sideways divide it into two wedge-shaped sections, of which the lower is the bony structure forming the skull and jaws, and the upper is a fatty mass entirely free from bones. Its broad forward end forms the expanded vertical surface of the forehead.

A quoin is not a standard geometric term. It belongs to pure nautical mathematics. I do not know that it has been defined before. A quoin is a solid which differs from a wedge in having its sharp end formed by the steep slant of one side, instead of the mutual tapering of both sides.

The lower section, called the junk, is one immense honeycomb of oil, formed by the crossing and recrossing, into ten thousand infiltrated cells, of tough elastic white fibers throughout its entire extent. The upper part, known as the Case, may be regarded as the great Heidelburgh Tun of the Sperm Whale. And as that famous vat in the German city was always kept full of the most excellent wine, and the residents of Heidelburgh might freely draw from it whenever they pleased, so the head of this leviathan, in its capped case, encloses the most precious of all his oils — the highly prized spermaceti, in its absolutely pure, limpid, and odoriferous state.

I do not know with what fine and costly material the Heidelburgh Tun was coated within, but in supreme richness that coating could not possibly have compared with the silken, pearl-colored membrane, like the lining of a fine fur coat, forming the inner surface of the Sperm Whale's case.

It will have been seen that the Heidelburgh Tun of the Sperm Whale embraces the entire length of the entire top of the head. And since the head embraces one third of the whole length of the creature, then setting that length down at eighty feet for a good-sized whale, you have more than twenty-six feet for the depth of the Tun.

As in decapitating the whale, the operator's instrument is brought close to the spot where an entrance is later forced into the spermaceti magazine, he has to be uncommonly careful lest a careless, untimely stroke should breach the sanctuary and wastefully let out its invaluable contents.
Thus much being said, attend now, I ask you, to that marvelous and — in this particular instance — almost fatal operation whereby the Sperm Whale's great Heidelburgh Tun is tapped.
